Title: IAM inventory and preflight
User story / technical objective: Before writing code, inventory how identity and the permission catalogue really work in DEV so IADM-03 reads the truth and invents nothing.
Acceptance criteria: Writes docs/iadm/iadm-03/IAM_INVENTORY.md covering: where users, profiles, roles, permissions and grants live (table and column names) and how login becomes claims read by the gateway and services; the permission catalogue (total keys, count and full list by prefix adm01 to adm08, iadm01 to iadm08, others, with the service using each); the roles present (R01 to R39) with key counts, and the iadm* keys held by R01, R02, R03, R04 and R28; whether grant changes are recorded anywhere (table, audit or only migrations); whether the RBAC section 21.1 guards exist in code or data; which service migrations inserted keys and in what order; any existing delegation contract or storage; the IADM-02 settings that exist for validity or review cadence; how the first-admin appointment and the CADM-02 handover work today; where the RBAC v3.0 role-to-permission matrix lives in the repo; conventions of IADM-01 to IADM-08 (port after 8106, route prefix, key naming, schema naming, demo-persona pattern); which demo institutes and personas exist. No emails, passwords, tokens or personal data in the file. Anything not found is written TBC. Confirms the DB target is the DEV Supabase project.
Build default or status: Read-only; no code or DB change

Title: IADM-03 service scaffold
User story / technical objective: Create IADM-03 as a separate deployable Java service following the conventions found in the preflight.
Acceptance criteria: Service starts; health endpoint answers; gateway route registered with no collision (including legacy routes); exception handling and structured logging; no tokens, claims or personal data in logs; technical doc started. Port and route reported. IADM-03 is never called per request by other services.
Build default or status: Preflight value wins over any proposal

Title: IADM-03 permission keys and role mapping
User story / technical objective: Add IADM-03's own permission keys and map them to roles, additively.
Acceptance criteria: Keys follow the convention (iadm03.*): register and matrix view; holder-level view; grant request submit; grant review and approve; review campaign manage; delegation manage; service registration submit and approve; handover view. Mapping: Super Admin (R01) manage and the only approver; System Admin (R02) operate (validate, prepare, intake) but never approve; Institution Admin (R03) own institute only, request and view; College Admin (R04) request only; Auditor (R28) read-only; no other role gets any key. No wildcard, no key that applies a grant. Only an additive migration to the existing shared catalogue; no existing key, grant or role changed; legacy keys untouched; before and after evidence reported. Each denial tested.
Build default or status: Own keys only; this is the only database change to the shared catalogue

Title: Schema, tenant scoping and row-level security for IADM-03's own records
User story / technical objective: Create only records IADM-03 itself owns.
Acceptance criteria: Records: grant requests, grant decisions and change evidence, review campaigns and decisions, delegations, service registrations, and (only if preflight shows no existing source) a handover status record. NOT created: any copy of the permission catalogue, holders, role matrix or audit. Institute-scoped rows carry the institute; FORCE row-level security on every table; rollback script; before and after inventory of objects. Test: another institute's rows are never readable; missing or mismatched tenant context fails closed.
Build default or status: Register, holders and matrix are computed on request, never stored

Title: Shared audit integration with refusal
User story / technical objective: Record every governed operation through the shared audit and refuse when it cannot be recorded.
Acceptance criteria: Uses audit.log_event, no second audit store. Recorded: holder-level reads, role matrix reads, grant requests, decisions and record results, review decisions, delegation create, revoke and expiry, service registration steps, handover reads, and every denial (self-grant, self-approval, scope escalation, R04 direct grant, R28 mutation). Event holds actor, action, scope, record reference, before and after references and correlation id, never tokens or claims. If the event cannot be recorded the operation is refused and nothing is partly recorded. Test covers audit-unavailable.
Build default or status: If no reusable audit exists this is a blocker

Title: Inspect the permission-key register
User story / technical objective: As R01 or R02 I can inspect a read-only register of every permission key with its owning service and current holders.
Acceptance criteria: Search and filter by service, status, role and key text; every key in the live catalogue appears, with counts reconciling to the source. Legacy adm* keys show as legacy; iadm07 shows 11 keys; iadm08 shows 4 granted and the reserved manage key ungranted (these counts are checked against the live catalogue, and any difference is reported, not hidden). No create, edit or delete control. Holder-level reads are recorded in shared audit. Works on real live data.
Build default or status: Counts come from preflight, not from the blueprint

Title: Inspect the role-to-permission matrix
User story / technical objective: As an authorized viewer I can inspect the R01 to R39 role matrix.
Acceptance criteria: Shows each role's RBAC v3.0 posture, its effective permission keys and scope, and the source version; differences between the matrix and live grants are flagged; no implicit inheritance shown; read recorded in shared audit; no edit control.
Build default or status: R03 and R04 have no matrix view in V1

Title: Read access evidence without changing anything
User story / technical objective: As R28 Auditor I can read access evidence read-only.
Acceptance criteria: Can open the register, matrix and every request, decision, review, delegation and registration record plus audit evidence; any create, update, approve, delegate or export attempt returns 403; no export control or endpoint.
Build default or status: R28 platform-wide read-only unless preflight finds an audit-scope assignment

Title: Runtime enforcement is unaffected by IADM-03
User story / technical objective: As R01 I can verify that the gateway, services and row-level security keep enforcing access without calling IADM-03.
Acceptance criteria: Headed proof: with the IADM-03 service stopped, logging in and using another built service (for example IADM-06) still works for R01 and is still refused where it should be; code check shows no per-request call to IADM-03; stopping IADM-03 changes no other service's behaviour.
Build default or status: None

Title: Catalogue, holders and role-matrix read engine
User story / technical objective: Compute the permission register, holders and role matrix on request from the existing catalogue and the RBAC v3.0 matrix source.
Acceptance criteria: Read-only. Owning service derived from the key prefix (iadm01 to iadm08 give that service; adm* gives Legacy; anything else is flagged Unknown). Status per key: granted, ungranted-reserved, dormant, legacy, unknown. Holders and counts read live from the existing grant data; totals reconciled with a direct count in a test. Matrix posture compared with live grants and any difference flagged, never corrected. No writes to the catalogue, no stored snapshot. Query time is the last-verified time.
Build default or status: Blueprint's stored register, holder and projection records are not built; owner may overrule

Title: View and request access within my institute
User story / technical objective: As R03 Institution Admin I can view and request access only within my own institute.
Acceptance criteria: Sees own institute's holders (account reference, role, status; no emails or credentials), review status and own requests and decisions; submits a request with subject reference, requested role or key, scope, validity and reason; cannot approve, cannot apply, cannot see another institute (changed parameter refused, tested with a second institute).
Build default or status: BUILD DEFAULT scope: IADM-03 requests cover platform-level grants and grants beyond the requester's ceiling; routine in-institute assignments stay in their owning services (owner may overrule)

Title: Submit an access request only
User story / technical objective: As R04 College Admin I can submit an access request but cannot grant anything.
Acceptance criteria: Request is accepted within own college context and shows only its own status; every grant, admin, register and matrix endpoint returns 403; college-user administration stays in CADM-02.
Build default or status: Posture is request-only per the matrix reading in the blueprint; confirm the matrix cell at preflight

Title: Validate and prepare a grant-change diff
User story / technical objective: As R02 I can validate a grant request and prepare the before and after diff without approving it.
Acceptance criteria: Validation checks the key exists, the owning service, the scope, the ceiling rule, current holders, conflicts, duplicates and expiry; produces a diff; R02 approve attempt returns 403; the catalogue is untouched; audited.
Build default or status: None

Title: Approve or reject another account's request
User story / technical objective: As R01 I can independently approve or reject a grant request from another account.
Acceptance criteria: Decision needs a reason and an account different from the requester and the subject; R01 sees the validated before and after diff; approval ends as Recorded with the plain statement 'recorded, not applied'; rejected requests close; R02, R03, R04 and R28 cannot decide (403); audited.
Build default or status: None

Title: Reject self-grant, self-approval and scope escalation
User story / technical objective: As the system I reject self-grant, self-approval and scope escalation.
Acceptance criteria: API tests and headed run: requester approving own request refused; granting oneself a role or key refused; a request beyond the section 21.1 ceiling refused; assigning a role with more permissions than the assigner refused; R38 cannot use IADM-03 beyond R25 and R26 through STM-07; every refusal is written to shared audit.
Build default or status: One-account limits noted in the report

Title: Refuse when audit cannot be recorded
User story / technical objective: As the system I refuse a governed operation if shared audit cannot record it.
Acceptance criteria: With the DEMO audit-disabled switch, each governed operation (request, decision, review decision, delegation change, registration step, holder-level read) is refused with no partial record and recovers when the switch is off.
Build default or status: None

Title: Grant request workflow engine (record-only)
User story / technical objective: One engine for grant requests, validation, decisions and before and after evidence.
Acceptance criteria: States: Requested, Validated, Approved, Rejected, Recorded. Rules: requester differs from approver and from subject; an independently authenticated R01 account decides; R02 can validate and prepare but never approve; a role cannot assign a role holding more permissions than the assigner; section 21.1 grantor ceilings enforced (R01 to R02 and R03; R02 to technical service identities only; R03 to R04-R24, R28-R31, R33-R39 inside its institute, R25 and R26 only through STM-07; R04 within CADM ceiling; R38 to R25 and R26 only through STM-07; never R01 to R04, R27 or R31 by R38). Outcome of approval is Recorded, not applied: there is no apply endpoint or control. Before and after diff stored as evidence. Duplicate requests are detected. Never touches the existing catalogue.
Build default or status: BUILD DEFAULT record-only (D-03 OWNER-OPEN); also R01's own elevation needs a second R01 approver and may be partial with one demo R01 account

Actor / role: Super Admin (R01) creates; System Admin (R02) and R01 review
Title: Run an access review campaign
User story / technical objective: As a reviewer I can attest, revoke or flag access in a review campaign.
Acceptance criteria: R01 creates a campaign (scope, reviewers, due date); items show account reference, roles, keys, owning service, scope, grantor and validity; decisions: ATTEST; REVOKE creates a governed revocation request needing R01 approval and recorded like a grant change; EXCEPTION needs reason, owner and expiry; no response becomes Overdue, never silently attested; reviewer differs from the subject; 'last used' appears only if a trusted source exists. Cadence is read from IADM-02 if it has one, otherwise a DEMO ONLY runtime default; R03 can see status but not decide.
Build default or status: BUILD DEFAULT reviewers are R01 and R02

Actor / role: Super Admin (R01); Institution Admin (R03) within own scope
Title: Create a recorded, scoped, time-bound delegation
User story / technical objective: As an authorized delegator I can create a recorded delegation.
Acceptance criteria: Record holds delegator, delegate, permitted action, target service, scope no wider than the delegator's, start, expiry, reason and status; wildcard or open-ended delegation refused; the same actor cannot approve their own delegation; maximum validity comes from an IADM-02 setting if one exists, otherwise a DEMO ONLY runtime value (real policy OWNER-OPEN); status shown as Pending, Active, Expired or Revoked.
Build default or status: BUILD DEFAULT: IADM-03 holds its own delegation record unless preflight finds an existing contract

Title: Revoke or expire a delegation
User story / technical objective: As an authorized operator I can revoke or expire a delegation and a consumer can see it is no longer valid.
Acceptance criteria: Revocation by the delegator or R01 is audited; expiry is worked out when read; a read endpoint returns Active, Expired or Revoked for any consuming service; headed run shows the status flip. No existing service reads it yet, so 'consumers reject it' is proven only through the read endpoint and marked partial.
Build default or status: Partial by design until a consuming service adopts the status

Actor / role: System Admin (R02) validates; Super Admin (R01) approves; service owner submits
Title: Register a new service's permission keys
User story / technical objective: As a service owner I can register new permission keys through an additive manifest.
Acceptance criteria: Manifest holds service, owner, keys with action and scope meaning, role grant proposal by role code, impact on holders, migration reference, rollback reference, test and audit evidence; validation checks the naming convention, duplicate meaning and that it is additive only; R01 approves; the register then shows the service as registered with its evidence; IADM-03 never applies a migration, removes or renames a key, or touches legacy keys.
Build default or status: None

Actor / role: Super Admin (R01); System Admin (R02); Institution Admin (R03) own institute
Title: View first-admin handover status
User story / technical objective: As R01 I can see the first institute-admin appointment and the CADM-02 handover state.
Acceptance criteria: Read-only status per institute taken from existing records (appointment actor and time, scope, CADM-02 acceptance); R03 sees own institute only; no emails or credentials; no new appointment mechanism is created unless preflight proves none exists, in which case it is reported and this row is partial.
Build default or status: BUILD DEFAULT read-only (IADM-01 and CADM-02 already own the actions)

Title: Demo data check (no invention)
User story / technical objective: Make sure every screen shows real records using only existing identities.
Acceptance criteria: Reuse existing demo institutes and personas; invent no emails, identities or institutes; if a second institute persona is missing create it only by the existing pattern and report it; any seeded requests, reviews, delegations and registrations are DEMO ONLY labelled and removable.
Build default or status: None

Title: Failure, isolation and role test suite
User story / technical objective: Automated tests for roles, scope, ceilings, refusals and failures.
Acceptance criteria: Role tests for R01, R02, R03 (two institutes), R04, R28 and a role outside them that must be denied; ceiling matrix test for every grantor row; self-grant, self-approval and escalation refusals; no apply endpoint exists; no write ever reaches the permission catalogue (before and after snapshots equal); register totals reconcile; audit-unavailable refuses; log-leak check (no tokens, claims or credentials); tenant isolation with FORCE row-level security.
Build default or status: None

Title: Evidence pack and close-out
User story / technical objective: Prove the work is done the way the owner defined done.
Acceptance criteria: Headed run for every persona (R01, R02, R03 for two institutes, R04, R28) and every fault; test results; plain-language report; blueprint acceptance scenarios and RBAC checklist ticked with named evidence; before and after catalogue snapshot proving nothing existing changed; exact port, route, keys, event names; decisions D-01 to D-12 with what the build assumed; table of all 25 rows with target versus ACTUAL and the exact evidence (screenshot, test or audit row) for each. No row may be called Demo-verified without named evidence; partials marked honestly.
Build default or status: None
